name: Franklin Antonio Hall
provenance: Three classrooms across four retained floors: 1101/1450 and floor silhouettes from UCSD emergency plans; auditorium 1301 from the public 2024-09-17 FIS master-plan raster. Common room corners align the relative frames approximately; no metric or campus placement is claimed.

coordinateSystem.description: First-floor reference: one unit per ten rendered pixels. Other pages are approximately aligned by common-core walls; these units are not meters.
coordinateSystem.northNote: The emergency-plan and FIS raster north arrows both point page-up, but matching room walls requires about 90 degrees of rotation between them. True north is unresolved; only relative room alignment is retained.

notes: 1301 is traced from its named outer wall boundary, including rear central entry area; stepped seating, furniture, columns and door swings are not room walls. The separate 1301C, 1301BB, 1301A and 1301B spaces are excluded.
Simplified curved wall segments use straight chords; this is an approximate room footprint, not measured three-dimensional auditorium geometry.
Three exact first-floor classroom labels have reviewed polygons: 1101 and 1450 from the emergency plan, 1301 from the FIS raster.

Retained 1101 and 1450 footprints, all four existing floor objects except the supplemented L1 fields, and relative room coordinates remain intact; absolute north is unknown. No geographic position is added.

Registration controls fit within 0.022 relative units; independent checks show up to 0.964 units (9.64 pixels in the old 2400-pixel render). This reflects the simplified emergency-plan boundaries, especially gross 1450 corners, and limits positional accuracy.

Both source north arrows point page-up, but room-wall registration rotates the frames by about 90 degrees. The relative room frame is retained; northDeg is null because absolute compass alignment is unresolved.
FIS viewer imagery may be outdated; title-block revision 2024-09-17 is recorded and no newer CAD-vault export is claimed.

Three exact classroom keys, 1101, 1301 and 1450, have reviewed first-floor positions. The first two source types are documented separately in the room references.
All four previously browsable floors are retained with source-traced approximate silhouettes. Other rooms remain unmodeled.
The original Facilities layout is preserved unchanged. It had no room polygons and repeated the campus exterior footprint on every floor.

The campus exterior footprint has different southeast-wing angles from the floor diagrams, so a reliable uniform campus registration is not established. This supplement uses relative units and deliberately has no geo placement.
Floor alignment is approximate using matching common-core walls. Floor heights are illustrative. Small door recesses, external exit landings and columns are simplified.

The emergency-plan and FIS raster north arrows both point page-up, but matching room walls requires about 90 degrees of rotation between them. True north is unresolved; only relative room alignment is retained.
